newsitem.title: DENMARK: SAS on right course, but far to go - CEO.
newsitem.headline: SAS on right course, but far to go - CEO.

text.p: Scandinavian Airlines System (SAS) chief executive Jan Stenberg says that the group is on the right path to meeting its objectives of improved profitability and customer satisfaction but still has far to go.

Writing in summer greetings to staff he said that market research showed improved customer perceptions of the airline, owned jointly by the government of Denmark, Sweden and Norway and private investors.
"We are on the right road, we can be happy about much progress, but we have not come far enough and we still have far to go," he said.
SAS forecasts 1997 full-year pre-tax profits on a par with last year's 1.8 billion Swedish crowns, despite a first-quarter 1997 loss of 269 million.
"It might seem like a great challenge, (to meet the forecast) but we must not forget that even such a result is still insufficient," he said. --Steve Weizman, Copenhagen newsroom +45 33969650
